title: Toasted Cornflake Milk Soft Serve with Cornflake Crunch
summary: Creamy cornflake-infused soft serve with a toasted grain flavour, topped with crunchy caramelised cornflake shards.
equipment: baking tray lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Spread 100 g cornflakes on a baking tray lined with baking paper and bake at 150 °C for 15 min until lightly toasted; cool.

steps.title: Crunch
steps.text: Toss 30 g cornflakes with 15 g melted butter and 1 tbsp sugar, bake at 150 °C for 10-12 min until golden and crisp; cool and crush lightly.

steps.title: Infuse
steps.text: Heat 480 ml double cream and 360 ml whole milk in a saucepan until steaming. Take off the heat, stir in the toasted 100 g cornflakes and steep for 20 min.

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Strain, pressing the flakes with a ladle to wring out the milk but not forcing the mush through; discard flakes.

steps.title: Custard
steps.text: Return the cornflake cream to the pan with 100 g sugar, 30 g light brown sugar and ¼ tsp fine salt; warm until dissolved. Whisk 6 large egg yolks in a bowl, whisk in a ladle of the hot cream, then pour back into the pan. Cook over medium-low, stirring constantly, until it coats the spoon and reaches 77 °C.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Strain into a clean bowl, cool, cover and chill for at least 4 h or overnight.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve straight away for soft-serve texture, piped or swirled into bowls and topped with the crunch. Alternatively, freeze until firm.

tips: Toast the cornflakes lightly to develop a warm, toasted flavour without browning them too much
Press the cornflakes with a ladle rather than forcing them through the sieve to keep the custard smooth
Serve the soft serve immediately for the best texture, or freeze and serve later as a firmer ice cream
storage: Keep the chilled custard covered for up to 24 h before churning; serve soft serve immediately or freeze for later.
